1 En habes versionem Germanicam illorum duorum locorum a Carolo Dyroff
comiter nobis missam : 1o in notis Fluegeli ad Fihrist, II, p. 110 infra, quaedam
citantur quae Ibn al Qiftî secundum Apomasarem de ʿUmar ibn al Farruchân
astronomo et interprete tradit ; deinde Ibn al Qiftî († 646 hegirae = 1248 p. Chr. n.)
sic pergit (cf. edit. Lipperti, p. 242, 5) : “ Ferner erwähnt Abû Maʿšar im Kitâb
„ almudâkarât „ (i. e. fere “ Quaestiones et responsa „, cf. Dozy, Suppl. aux dict.
arab., I, 487 ; cui titulo addendum est “ de secretis astrologiae „, cf. locum
Albiruni supra citatum). “ das Shâdân ibn Baḥr (? : nomen patris Dyroffio cor-
„ ruptum videtur) “ verfasst hat, dass al Faḍl ibn Sahl, genannt dû ʾlrijâsatain,
„ der Vezier des Al Maʿmûn, den ʿUmar ibn al Farruchân aus seinem Wohnort
„ herbeirief und mit al Maʿmûn bekannt machte, worauf er (für Maʿmûn) viele
„ Bücher übersetzte und iudicia aufstellte, die sich noch heute im Reichsarchiv
„ vorfinden „ etc. — 2o Ibn Abî Uṣaibiʿa († 668 hegirae = 1269 p. Chr. n.), I, p. 207,
in capitulo de Alkindî init., eius versionibus Arabicis laudatis, haec scribit :
“ Abû Maʿšar sagt im Kitâb almudâkarât, das Shâdân verfasst hat : Die besten
„ Uebesetzer im Islâm sind diese vier : Ḥunain ibn Isḥâq, Jaʿqûb ibn Isḥâq al
„ Kindî, Ṯâbit ibn Qurra al Ḥarrânî und ʿUmar ibn al Farruchân al Ṭabarî „.
2 Ed. Browne, A hand-list of the Muham. manuscripts in Cambridge, 1900,
no 1208.
3 Quat. f, fol. 3 ss. in editione Veneta anni 1506 (Introductorium in astronomiam
Albumasaris Albalachi, Venetiis, expensis Melchionis Sessa) quam bibliothecae

p. 703, no 3825.
sections.en:
1 Behold you have the German version of those two passages by Carolus Dyroff
courteously sent to us: 1st in the notes of Fluegel to the Fihrist, II, p. 110 below, certain things
are cited which Ibn al Qiftî hands down according to Apomasar concerning ʿUmar ibn al Farruchân
the astronomer and interpreter; then Ibn al Qiftî († 646 of the hegira = 1248 A.D.)
proceeds thus (cf. edit. of Lippert, p. 242, 5): “ Furthermore Abû Maʿšar mentions in the Kitâb
„ almudâkarât „ (i. e. roughly “ Questions and answers „, cf. Dozy, Suppl. aux dict.
arab., I, 487; to which title must be added “ on the secrets of astrology „, cf. the passage
of Albiruni cited above). “ that Shâdân ibn Baḥr (? : the father's name seems corrupt to Dyroff)
„ has composed, that al Faḍl ibn Sahl, called dû ʾlrijâsatain,
„ the vizier of Al Maʿmûn, summoned ʿUmar ibn al Farruchân from his dwelling place
„ and made him acquainted with al Maʿmûn, whereupon he translated many
„ books (for Maʿmûn) and set up iudicia, which are still found today in the imperial archive
„ „ etc. — 2nd Ibn Abî Uṣaibiʿa († 668 of the hegira = 1269 A.D.), I, p. 207,
in the chapter on Alkindî at the beginning, his Arabic versions having been praised, writes these things:
“ Abû Maʿšar says in the Kitâb almudâkarât, which Shâdân has composed: The best
„ translators in Islâm are these four: Ḥunain ibn Isḥâq, Jaʿqûb ibn Isḥâq al
„ Kindî, Ṯâbit ibn Qurra al Ḥarrânî and ʿUmar ibn al Farruchân al Ṭabarî „.
2 Ed. Browne, A hand-list of the Muham. manuscripts in Cambridge, 1900,
no 1208.
3 Quat. f, fol. 3 ss. in the Venetian edition of the year 1506 (Introductorium in astronomiam
Albumasaris Albalachi, Venetiis, expensis Melchionis Sessa) which the prefect of the Munich
library most generously lent to me.
4 Suter, Mathem. und Astron. der Araber, p. 29; Houzeau et Lancaster, op. cit.,
p. 703, no 3825.

summary.headline: Shādhān’s Compilation of Apomasar
summary.text: Discussion of Abū Saʿīd Shādhān’s Greek “Mysteries” as a compilation of Apomasar’s posthumous discourses, conversations, and excerpts. The analysis identifies borrowed chapters on the decans, astrological chorography, the seven planets, and other sections of Apomasar’s “Greater Introduction,” while noting the work on the secrets of the stars.
